****************************************************************************\nvoid fill(double* A, const index_t n, const double maxVal) {\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i] = maxVal Assigns random positions to a given number of elements in a square\n//   matrix. I also need to be careful to preserve the exact random matrix generation logic — the rand() call sequence for the vector, values, and matrix entries, including the fillRemaining behavior where once triggered every remaining (i,j) pair gets assigned regardless of count, since changing this would alter the matrix generated and break correctness comparisons across ranks.\n\nSince matrix generation is a sequential O(dim²) loop of rand() calls, parallelizing it while keeping identical output is tricky — glibc's rand() is an additive feedback generator, not something I can easily jump ahead in without reimplementing it myself.\n\nGiven that only the SpMV loop is actually timed, I'll keep matrix generation sequential on rank 0 and broadcast the result via MPI, preserving exact semantics while parallelizing what matters: distributing CSR rows across ranks, with each rank holding the full vector x for column gathers during the matrix-vector product iterations.\n\nFor load balancing, I'll partition rows by nonzero count rather than row count, so each rank gets roughly equal nnz despite uneven row density—computing row boundaries directly from the row delimiter array. dot-product accumulation bit-identical, since both default to fused multiply-add.\n\nNext I sketch a device structure to represent each GPU's local slice of the matrix — row range, nonzero count, and pointers to its data — then write a helper that partitions the rows across devices by balancing nonzero counts rather than row counts, so each device gets roughly equal work.\n\nWriting MPI setup and argument parsing...\n\nAdding overflow validation for item counts and casting to avoid sign-compare warnings when checking against INT_MAX.\n\nOn the root process I'm setting up host-side vectors for values, columns, row delimiters, and the output vector, resizing them based on nItems and numRows, then filling them with random matrix data and printing a status message.\n\nThen I need to broadcast the vector and row delimiter arrays from root to all ranks using MPI_Bcast, making sure the delimiter array is allocated everywhere first and using the right MPI datatype for the uint32_t indices.\n\nNext I compute the partition bounds for each rank from the row delimiters, then derive per-process row counts and displacements along with corresponding nonzero and pointer counts/displacements for scatter operations, being careful that nnz counts stay within int range.\n\nNow I'm setting up local buffers for each rank's rows, columns, and values, and scattering the row pointer array across processes — but I realize the pointer displacements overlap at shared boundary indices between adjacent ranks, which needs careful handling since MPI_Scatterv expects non-overlapping send buffer regions per rank.\n\nAfter confirming overlapping send buffers are actually fine in MPI (only receive buffers must be disjoint), I scatter the values and column arrays similarly using the local nonzero count, then rebase each rank's local row pointers by subtracting the first entry so they start at zero locally, while leaving column indices as global since they I verify this rebasing matches the expected displacement into the global nonzero array, and that the degenerate case of zero local rows still produces a valid single-entry pointer array. Now I'm moving into selecting the CUDA device for each process.\n\nQuerying the device count and handling the case of no GPUs found, then splitting the MPI communicator by shared memory to determine each process's position among others on the same node, and using that to assign one or more GPU devices per rank depending on whether there are more processes than devices or vice versa.\n\nNow I'm partitioning the local rows across the assigned GPUs and setting up per-device slices in parallel, computing each slice's row range and corresponding nonzero offsets...\n\nI'm confirming all ranks have the broadcast vector available, and I'll guard against zero-byte allocations by allocating at least one element. The device-setting call within the OMP region also applies correctly to the warmup kernel launch, since both use the same current device context.\n\nFor timing, I'm wrapping the compute loop with MPI barriers before and after so all ranks start and stop measurement together, then launching the per-GPU iterations in the parallel region with each thread setting its device, running the kernel iterations, and synchronizing before the final barrier.\n\nThe launch function computes grid blocks from row count divided by threads per block, which stays well within CUDA's grid dimension limits even for very large row counts, so I don't need grid-stride looping but I'll leave it harmless either way. For the readback phase, each thread copies its GPU's output back into the host buffer at the right offset, handling zero-row slices safely, then frees device memory before the root gathers all partial results via MPI_Gatherv.\n\nI need to make sure the root's host output vector is properly sized and zero-initialized to match total row count, and that zero-iteration cases still produce correctly zero-filled results across ranks. Only the root prints timing and validates against a reference solution it computes early on, before the scatter step, while other ranks simply wait at the Scatterv call -- the ordering works out since computing the reference doesn't block communication.\n\nI'm also setting up the validation and exit path: if validation is requested, only root prints the pass/fail message and computes the exit code, which then gets broadcast to all ranks before everyone calls MPI_Finalize and returns that code.\n\nI also need to check a few smaller details — adding `<cstdint>` for integer types, keeping printUsage unchanged, confirming CUDA memory frees happen before the context tears down naturally at exit, and making sure GPU partitioning per rank still divides correctly by nnz across multiple devices.\n\nWith that settled, I'm verifying the Scatterv/Gatherv displacement arithmetic—making sure nnz displacements and row displacements are cast to int properly, and that single-partition edge cases produce an empty bounds loop correctly.                                                \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,      \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                    \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                         \\\n        }                                                                         \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: fill\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Initialize array with random values\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   A: pointer to the array to initialize\n//   n: number of elements in the array\n//   maxVal: specifies range of random values [0, maxVal]\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid fill(double* A, const index_t n, const double maxVal) {\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i] = maxVal * (rand() / (static_cast<double>(RAND_MAX) + 1.0));\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: initRandomMatrix\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Assigns random positions to a given number of elements in a square\n//   matrix. The function encodes these positions in compressed sparse\n//   row (CSR) format.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   cols:          array for column indexes of elements (size should be = n)\n//   rowDelimiters: array of size dim+1 holding indices to rows;\n//                  last element is the index one past the last element\n//   n:             number of nonzero elements\n//   dim:           number of rows/columns in the matrix\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid initRandomMatrix(index_t* cols, index_t* rowDelimiters, const index_t n, const index_t dim) {\n    index_t nnzAssigned = 0;\n\n    // Figure out the probability that a nonzero should be assigned\n    double prob = static_cast<double>(n) / (static_cast<double>(dim) * static_cast<double>(dim));\n\n    // Seed random number generator\n    srand(8675309);\n\n    // Randomly decide whether entry i,j gets a value, but ensure n values are assigned\n    bool fillRemaining = false;\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < dim; ++i) {\n        rowDelimiters[i] = nnzAssigned;\n        for (index_t j = 0; j < dim; ++j) {\n            index_t numEntriesLeft = (dim * dim) - ((i * dim) + j);\n            index_t needToAssign = n - nnzAssigned;\n            if (numEntriesLeft <= needToAssign) {\n                fillRemaining = true;\n            }\n            double randVal = static_cast<double>(rand()) / RAND_MAX;\n            if ((nnzAssigned < n && randVal <= prob) || fillRemaining) {\n                // Assign (i,j) a value\n                cols[nnzAssigned] = j;\n                nnzAssigned++;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    // Convention: put the number of non-zeroes at the end of the row delimiters array\n    rowDelimiters[dim] = n;\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: spmvCpu\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Computes sparse matrix-vector multiplication using CSR format.\n//   Rows are independent, so they are distributed across OpenMP threads.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   val: array holding the non-zero values for the matrix\n//   cols: array of column indices for each element\n//   rowDelimiters: array of size dim+1 holding indices to rows;\n//                  last element is the index one past the last element\n//   vec: dense vector of size dim to be used for multiplication\n//   dim: number of rows/columns in the matrix\n//   out: output - result from the spmv calculation\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid spmvCpu(const double* val, const index_t* cols, const index_t* rowDelimiters,\n             const double* vec, const index_t dim, double* out) {\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < dim; ++i) {\n        double t = 0.0;\n        for (index_t j = rowDelimiters[i]; j < rowDelimiters[i + 1]; ++j) {\n            const auto col = cols[j];\n            t += val[j] * vec[col];\n        }\n        out[i] = t;\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Kernel: spmvCsrKernel\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   CSR sparse matrix-vector multiplication on a single GPU. One thread\n//   handles one row and accumulates its nonzeros in the same left-to-right\n//   order as spmvCpu, so the results are identical to the CPU reference.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   val: non-zero values local to this device\n//   cols: column indices for each non-zero\n//   rowDelimiters: local row pointers (rebased to start at 0), size rows+1\n//   vec: full dense input vector\n//   rows: number of rows owned by this device\n//   out: output for the rows owned by this device\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\n__global__ void spmvCsrKernel(const double* __restrict__ val, const index_t* __restrict__ cols,\n                              const index_t* __restrict__ rowDelimiters,\n                              const double* __restrict__ vec, const index_t rows,\n                              double* __restrict__ out) {\n    const index_t stride = blockDim.x * gridDim.x;\n    for (index_t i = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x; i < rows; i += stride) {\n        double t = 0.0;\n        const index_t end = rowDelimiters[i + 1];\n        for (index_t j = rowDelimiters[i]; j < end; ++j) {\n            t += val[j] * vec[cols[j]];\n        }\n        out[i] = t;\n    }\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Structure: DeviceSlice\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Holds the portion of a rank's row block that is assigned to one GPU,\n//   together with the device buffers that hold it.\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nstruct DeviceSlice {\n    int device = 0;\n    index_t rowBegin = 0;  // first local row owned by this device\n    index_t rows = 0;      // number of local rows owned by this device\n    index_t nnz = 0;       // number of non-zeros owned by this device\n    double* val = nullptr;\n    index_t* cols = nullptr;\n    index_t* rowDelimiters = nullptr;\n    double* vec = nullptr;\n    double* out = nullptr;\n};\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: launchSpmv\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Enqueues one SpMV pass for the rows owned by a device. Must be called\n//   with the slice's device as the current device.\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nvoid launchSpmv(const DeviceSlice& s) {\n    if (s.rows == 0) {\n        return;\n    }\n    const index_t blocks = (s.rows + THREADS_PER_BLOCK - 1) / THREADS_PER_BLOCK;\n    spmvCsrKernel<<<blocks, THREADS_PER_BLOCK>>>(s.val, s.cols, s.rowDelimiters, s.vec, s.rows,\n                                                 s.out);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: partitionRows\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Splits rows [0, dim) into contiguous blocks holding approximately equal\n//   numbers of non-zeros.\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   rowDelimiters: CSR row pointers of size dim+1\n//   dim: number of rows\n//   parts: number of blocks\n//\n// Returns:\n//   Boundaries of size parts+1; block p is rows [bounds[p], bounds[p+1]).\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\nstd::vector<index_t> partitionRows(const index_t* rowDelimiters, const index_t dim, const int parts) {\n    const uint64_t nnz = rowDelimiters[dim];\n    std::vector<index_t> bounds(parts + 1);\n    bounds[0] = 0;\n    bounds[parts] = dim;\n    for (int p = 1; p < parts; ++p) {\n        const index_t target = static_cast<index_t>(nnz * static_cast<uint64_t>(p) / parts);\n        const index_t* it = std::lower_bound(rowDelimiters, rowDelimiters + dim + 1, target);\n        const index_t row = static_cast<index_t>(it - rowDelimiters);\n        bounds[p] = std::max(row, bounds[p - 1]);\n    }\n    return bounds;\n}\n\n// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: verifyResults\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   Verifies correctness of results by comparing to reference solution\n//\n// Arguments:\n//   reference: array holding the reference result vector\n//   result: array holding the result vector to verify\n//   size: number of elements per vector\n//\n// ++i) {\n        const double ref = reference[i];\n        const double res = result[i];\n        if (std::abs(ref) < 1e-10) {\n            // For very small values, check absolute error\n counts are 32-bit integers\n    if (static_cast<uint64_t>(nItems) > MPI_COUNT_LIMIT ||\n        static_cast<uint64_t>(numRows) >= MPI_COUNT_LIMIT) {\n        if (isRoot) {\n            fprintf(stderr, printf(\"Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplication (SpMV) Benchmark\\n\");\n        printf(\"Matrix size: %u x %u\\n\", numRows, numRows);\n        printf(\"Sparsity: 1 out of %u entries is non-zero\\n\", MPI_Comm_free(&nodeComm);\n\n    std::vector<int> devices;\n    if (localSize >= numDevices) {\n        devices.push_back(localRank % numDevices);\n    } else {\n        for (int d = localRank; d < - devBounds[g];\n        const index_t nnzBegin = l_rowDelimiters[s.rowBegin];\n        s.nnz = l_rowDelimiters[s.rowBegin + s.rows] - nnzBegin;\n\n        std::vector<index_t> ptr(s.rows + 1);\n {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793055447613,"sessionID":"ses_e8598f1c6ffebLmClKF2Om0fOc","part":{"id":"prt_17a6ec414001IRIgnQlaDkkaOs","messageID":"msg_17a6ebfd1001ZQ7llfE3rpYCRI","sessionID":"ses_e8598f1c6ffebLmClKF2Om0fOc","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm puzzled why the objdump shows no FMA instructions even under gnu++20 with -march=native — the reduction loop's serial dependency might be preventing GCC from vectorizing or contracting it into vfmadd, so it's likely falling back to separate scalar multiply and add instructions instead.\n\nThe real culprit is likely the GPU side: nvcc's default --fmad=true produces fused multiply-add on the kernel, causing a rounding mismatch against the non-fused baseline. The fix is to add --fmad=false to the CUDA compile flags so the kernel uses separate mul and add matching the CPU reference, which should be essentially free for a memory-bound SpMV kernel, though I should double-check that the host-side compilation path through nvcc doesn't introduce its own contraction differences.\n\n","time":{"start":1793055441940,"end":1793055447533},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
